passages.text: Binary search requires a sorted array. Use the half-open interval [lo, hi): lo is included and hi is excluded. Initialize lo to zero and hi to the array length.

sources.quote: Binary search requires a sorted array. Use the half-open interval [lo, hi): lo is included and hi is excluded. Initialize lo to zero and hi to the array length.

passages.text: While lo is less than hi, set mid to lo plus floor((hi - lo) / 2). If array[mid] equals the target, return mid. If array[mid] is smaller, set lo to mid + 1. Otherwise set hi to mid. If the loop ends without a match, return -1.

passages.text: Find 12 in [2, 5, 8, 12, 16]. With lo = 0 and hi = 5, mid = 2 gives 8, so lo becomes 3. Next mid = 4 gives 16, so hi becomes 4. Next mid = 3 gives 12. Return index 3.

blocks.topic: Binary Search Time and Space Complexity

passages.text: With constant-time array indexing, worst-case search time is O(log n), because each iteration roughly halves the interval. This iterative version uses O(1) auxiliary space. Sorting cost is excluded from that search-only runtime.

passages.text: Dijkstra's algorithm requires nonnegative edge weights, with zero-weight edges being permitted but negative edge weights not supported.

sources.quote: Dijkstra's algorithm works with negative edge weights.
Correction: I misspoke. The standard Dijkstra algorithm requires nonnegative edge weights. Zero-weight edges are allowed. Do not write that negative edges are supported.

passages.text: Relaxing an edge (u, v) involves checking if the current distance to v can be improved by taking the path through u: if dist[u] + weight(u, v) < dist[v], then update dist[v] to this candidate distance and set predecessor[v] to u.

sources.quote: Relaxing an edge (u, v) means checking whether dist[u] + weight(u, v) is smaller than dist[v]. If it is, update dist[v] to that candidate distance and set predecessor[v] to u.
